name: Hittle Bottom Campground
note: BLM Moab Field Office campground on the banks of the Colorado River along SR-128, ~23 mi from Moab; a popular river-trip launch. 15 individual sites (first-come, first-served) + 1 reservable group site; 5 sites fit RVs up to 40 ft; vault toilets, no water/hookups. Group site reservable online; individual sites FCFS. --Claude

name: Arches National Park - Devils Garden Campground
note: The only campground in Arches NP, 18 mi from the entrance near the Devils Garden trailhead (~5,200 ft) amid sandstone fins. 51 sites (incl 2 group + 1 accessible); individual sites vary in size, fitting RVs from ~25 up to 40 ft; flush toilets, drinking water, no hookups or dump station. Reservable online Mar-Oct (six-month window); FCFS Nov-Feb. --Claude

name: Gooseberry Campground
note: Fishlake NF campground in the Gooseberry area ~18 mi from Salina (accessed off I-70, ~7,850 ft) in aspen/conifer forest. 13 sites (2 pull-through) plus a group pavilion; vault toilets, potable water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Dewey Bridge Campground
note: BLM Moab Field Office campground on the Colorado River along SR-128 (Upper Colorado River Scenic Byway), ~29 mi NE of the US-191 junction. 8 individual sites (tents/small RVs, first-come first-served, $20) plus 3 reservable group sites; vault toilets, fire rings, shade shelters, boat ramp, no water/hookups/dump. Individual sites FCFS; group sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Maple Grove Campground
note: Fishlake National Forest (Fillmore RD) campground beneath red cliffs on Ivie Creek, ~4 mi W of US-50 on FR-101 (milepost 146). Several single sites first-come first-served plus 3 reservable group sites; vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Maple/cottonwood/oak shade; Rock Canyon Trail starts in the campground. --Claude

name: San Rafael Swinging Bridge Campground
note: BLM San Rafael Swell Recreation Area campground at the historic Swinging Bridge where Buckhorn Wash meets the San Rafael River, ~20 mi of graded dirt road S of I-70/Buckhorn Draw. Three loops: Swinging Bridge North (6), Equestrian loop (6, with corrals), Swinging Bridge South (11); all first-come first-served, picnic tables/fire rings/vault toilets, no water or trash service. General campground (offers a horse loop). --Claude

name: Joes Valley Reservoir Campground
note: Manti-La Sal NF (Ferron/Price RD) developed campground near Joes Valley Reservoir at ~7,000 ft, on the Wasatch Plateau ~18 mi W of Orangeville via SR-29. ~51 standard nonelectric single/double-family sites; paved roads and parking spurs, vault toilets, drinking water. Sites 1-7 first-come, first-served; remaining sites reservable online. Note: recreation.gov flags a 2026 construction closure window. --Claude Rechecked 2026-09-30: open (recreation.gov shows late-September 2026 sites reserved/available). --Claude

name: Oak Creek Campground (Oak City)
note: Fishlake NF (Fillmore RD) campground in Oak Creek Canyon ~4.4 mi E of Oak City, ~6,000 ft, shaded by oak/maple/cottonwood along Oak Creek. 17 individual sites (upper and lower loops) plus 4 group sites; picnic tables, fire rings, grills, vault toilets, drinking water, amphitheater/play field. Individual sites first-come, first-served (pay on arrival); group sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Potters Pond Campground
note: Manti-La Sal NF campground in Upper Joes Valley next to two ponds at ~9,000 ft, reached via the well-maintained dirt/gravel Miller Flat Rd (car/RV accessible). Single, double and equestrian sites; per recreation.gov various sites take RVs up to 25, 30, or 40 ft. Tables and fire rings with grills, vault toilets, no drinking water/electricity/trash. Some sites reservable online, remainder first-come, first-served. Arapeen OHV trail access. --Claude

name: Chicken Creek Campground
note: Manti-La Sal NF (Sanpete RD) primitive campground in Chicken Creek Canyon, ~4 mi SE of Levan on Forest Rd 101, at ~6,200 ft. 8 shady pine sites with fire pits and picnic tables; no potable water. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Good creek fishing; Yuba State Park nearby. --Claude

name: Lake Canyon Recreation Area Campground
note: USFS Manti-La Sal NF Lake Canyon Rec Area off SR-31/Skyline Dr, ~18 mi east of Fairview between Huntington and Cleveland reservoirs; ~50 first-come single sites plus 5 reservable group sites and 4 reservable double sites (#11,17,24,41), vault toilets, no water/hookups; popular OHV area. Group/double sites reservable online, rest first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Gooseberry Campground (Manti-La Sal)
note: USFS Manti-La Sal NF on an aspen-covered hillside above Gooseberry Reservoir, ~1 mi north on FDR 124 off SR-31; 10 first-come single sites plus a reservable group site, vault toilets and potable water, pack-in/pack-out, no hookups. Group site reservable online; singles first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Ponderosa (Uinta NF)
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Spanish Fork RD, in Bear Canyon just off the Nebo Loop Scenic Byway at ~6200 ft; 23 single-family sites with paved roads and parking spurs, vault toilets and drinking water. Salt Creek runs alongside (rainbow trout). Mix of reservable and first-come-first-served sites, reservable online. --Claude

name: Fish Creek (Manti-La Sal NF)
note: Manti-La Sal NF, Price RD, within the Spanish Fork-Scofield Recreation Area ~2.5 mi W of Scofield Reservoir at ~7720 ft; small remote 6-8 site horse-friendly campground beside Fish Creek with vault toilet, picnic tables, fire rings and a horse corral, no water (pack-in/pack-out). First-come, first-served (pay via recreation.gov app QR at the site). Drive-in loop; small/primitive rigs. --Claude

name: Avintaquin Campground
note: Ashley NF atop Indian Canyon off US-191 between Duchesne and Helper at ~9000 ft among Douglas fir; several single-family sites plus one group site (#10), RVs to 30 ft, vault toilets and no water (bring your own). Access is narrow washboard gravel with a hill climb. For the 2026 season the family sites are first-come-first-served; the group site remains reservable online. --Claude

name: Blackhawk (Uinta NF)
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Spanish Fork RD, on the Nebo Loop Scenic Byway (Payson Canyon) at ~8000 ft; large ~38-site campground with paved roads and spurs, flush toilets, drinking water and a dump station. Has an equestrian loop (Loop E) plus group and single/double family sites (a general campground open to all, not horse-only). No hookups. Reservable online with some single-family sites first-come-first-served. --Claude

name: Tinney Flat Campground
note: Small USFS campground (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Spanish Fork RD) in Santaquin Canyon just off the Nebo Loop Scenic Byway, ~7,050 ft; ~10 single sites plus 3 group sites, standard nonelectric, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Santaquin Canyon Rd (FR 14) is paved but steep and narrow -- not recommended for large rigs but a 23-ft rig can get in. Both reservable and FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Payson Lakes Campground
note: Large USFS campground (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Spanish Fork RD) on the Nebo Loop Scenic Byway ~12 mi up Payson Canyon, ~8,000 ft; ~90 single/double sites in loops A/B/C plus 3 group sites and 2 yurts. A loop is FCFS all season, other loops reservable (5+ days ahead); paved roads, vault/flush toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Adjacent to Big East Lake. --Claude

name: Simpson Springs Campground
note: BLM Pony Express NHT campground on the Pony Express Backcountry Byway ~12 mi S of Dugway; 20 drive-in sites (many compacted-gravel pull-throughs), vault toilets, seasonal potable water, no hookups. Sites 1-10 reservable on recreation.gov, sites 11-19 first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Diamond Campground (Diamond Fork Canyon)
note: USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache, Spanish Fork RD) campground in Diamond Fork Canyon along Diamond Fork/Sixth Water creek at ~5,200 ft; 38 single + 22 double family sites plus group sites, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; paved access. Reservable on recreation.gov with some FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Sawmill Hollow Campground (Diamond Fork)
note: Small primitive USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache, Spanish Fork RD) campground in upper Diamond Fork Canyon at ~6,200 ft; 4 drive-in gravel sites, vault toilet, no water, no hookups; First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Reached via paved Diamond Fork Rd then a short gravel spur; satellite shows a graded gravel loop with pull-offs that fits a 23-ft rig. --Claude

Fees: requires 3-Day U-W-C NF Pass ($10/stay per vehicle, 2 nights); not needed with an America the Beautiful interagency pass or a U-W-C NF 7-day ($20) or annual ($60) pass

name: Cherry Campground (Hobble Creek)
note: USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache, Spanish Fork RD) campground on Hobble Creek ~6 mi from Springville at ~5,200 ft; 14 single/double drive-in sites with paved spurs and cement pads (first-come, first-served), plus 4 reservable group tent sites; vault toilets, NO potable water (bring your own), no hookups (RVs welcome self-contained). Group sites reservable on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Pelican Lake Campground
note: BLM (Vernal FO) campground on Pelican Lake near Randlett at ~4,800 ft; 13 sites (3 group-size) on a drive-in loop, vault toilets, boat ramp; no hookups. First-come, first-served (Scan & Pay via recreation.gov app), $35 group. Bluegill and bass fishing. --Claude

name: Balsam Campground (Hobble Creek Canyon)
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF campground in Hobble Creek Canyon ~12 mi E of Springville (~6,000 ft), along Hobble Creek. 26 sites: 11 standard nonelectric (drive-in), 14 tent-only, 2 group; vault toilets, no potable water (bring your own). Paved canyon-road access. Reservable online with some first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Hope Campground (Squaw Peak Road)
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF campground ~5 mi up Squaw Peak Road above Provo Canyon (~6,500 ft), forested in maple/scrub oak/fir. 24 single family sites, vault toilets, no water on site. Reservable online with some first-come, first-served. Squaw Peak Road is narrow, steep and winding; vehicles/trailers over 30 ft not recommended (a 23-ft rig fits). --Claude

name: Clover Springs Campground (BLM)
note: BLM Salt Lake Field Office campground in the Onaqui Mountains foothills near Dugway (~6,000 ft), on a spring-fed stream lined with cottonwoods. 10 individual sites (first-come, first-served) plus one reservable group site; 2 sites are equestrian-capable. Vault toilets, no potable water; max equipment length 30 ft. Individual sites first-come, first-served; group site reservable online. --Claude

name: Green River Campground (Dinosaur National Monument)
note: NPS Dinosaur National Monument campground on a cottonwood-shaded bench along the Green River below Split Mountain (~4,800 ft), ~5 mi E of the dinosaur quarry. 80 sites for tents/RVs up to 75 ft; drinking water and flush toilets, no hookups/dump station and RVs cannot fill tanks. Apr-Oct; Loop B reservable mid-May to mid-Sep, Loops A and C first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Upper Narrows Campground (South Willow Canyon)
note: Small primitive USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Salt Lake RD) campground in South Willow Canyon, Stansbury Mtns, ~6,900 ft; 6 single drive-in sites (plus 2 group sites, one walk-to) dispersed along the canyon road, vault toilet, no water. Willow Creek runs alongside. Upper South Willow Canyon Rd is narrow, rough gravel, not recommended for trailers -- best for tents and small self-contained rigs, but drive-in and not 4WD-required. Reservable online (some FCFS). --Claude

name: Lower Narrows Campground (South Willow Canyon)
note: Small primitive USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Salt Lake RD) campground in South Willow Canyon, Stansbury Mtns; 3 single drive-in sites with Willow Creek running alongside, vault toilet, no water. Upper South Willow Canyon Rd is narrow, rough gravel, not recommended for trailers -- best for tents and small self-contained rigs, drive-in and not 4WD-required. Mix of FCFS and reservable online. --Claude

name: Yellowstone Campground (Ashley NF)
note: Ashley NF campground on the banks of the Yellowstone River (Yellowstone Rd #119 above Mountain Home), ~40 mi from Duchesne; one reservable group site (to 40 people, 4 RV/trailers) plus several first-come, first-served single sites ($10/night) at ~7,700 ft. Group site reservable on recreation.gov; singles FCFS. --Claude

name: Bridge Campground (Yellowstone River)
note: Small Ashley NF campground adjacent to the Yellowstone River, just below the river bridge on Yellowstone Rd #119 above Mountain Home, at ~7,600 ft. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov for reservations). --Claude

name: Tanners Flat Campground
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF in Little Cottonwood Canyon at ~7,200 ft, 6 mi up from Sandy. 31 single + 3 double + 4 group sites plus amphitheater, no hookups; site max lengths listed 9-80 ft but the narrow canyon road makes rigs over ~28 ft tight (reviewer caution). Reservable plus some first-come, first-served sites. --Claude

name: Lower Provo River Campground
note: USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Heber-Kamas RD) campground on the Mirror Lake Scenic Byway (UT-150) ~10.6 mi E of Kamas, along the Lower Provo River at ~7,400 ft. 10 single sites with tables/fire rings, vault toilets, no potable water (bring water). Reservable on recreation.gov (some FCFS). Mirror Lake rec pass required. --Claude

name: Swift Creek Campground (Ashley NF)
note: USFS (Ashley NF) campground at the end of Yellowstone Rd (FR 119) ~11 mi N of Mountain Home, on the Yellowstone River near the Swift Creek confluence and the High Uintas Wilderness boundary, ~8,100 ft. Basic drive-in sites with vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Gravel access road. --Claude

name: Whiterocks Campground
note: USFS (Ashley NF) campground up Whiterocks Canyon on FR 492 (~7 mi N of Whiterocks, then in on gravel), along the Whiterocks River at ~7,500 ft. 21 sites, max RV ~30 ft, tables and vault toilets, no potable water (recently rebuilt with native rock, primitive). First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Uinta Canyon Campground (Ashley NF)
note: Ashley NF campground along the Uinta River on Forest Road 118, ~3 mi past the pavement (North Uinta Canyon). 24 sites (1 tent + 23 single units), vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). High Uintas Wilderness trailhead and trout fishing nearby. --Claude

name: Paradise Park Campground (Ashley NF)
note: Ashley NF campground on the shore of Paradise Park Reservoir, ~40 mi NW of Vernal via UT-121 and Forest Road 104, elev ~9,800 ft. 15 sites, max RV ~25 ft, vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Rainbow trout fishing; rustic guard station rentable separately. --Claude

name: Pole Creek Lake Campground (Ashley NF)
note: Small primitive Ashley NF campground a short walk from Pole Creek Lake in the Uinta Mtns, elev ~10,000 ft. 18 sites on a dirt-road loop, vault toilets, no water/power. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Access is Forest Road 117, steep and winding in places -- fine for a 23-ft rig but not large RVs/trailers; not 4WD-required. --Claude

name: Trial Lake Campground
note: USFS campground on Trial Lake off the Mirror Lake Scenic Byway (SR-150), Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, ~9,500 ft. ~60 paved single sites (one double), picnic tables and fire rings; vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups. RVs over 30 ft may drag on the spillway (23-ft rig fine). Reservable online; some sites FCFS before the reservation window opens. --Claude

name: Butterfly Lake Campground
note: USFS campground on Butterfly Lake off the Mirror Lake Scenic Byway (SR-150), Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, ~10,300 ft. 20 single sites, unpaved roads/spurs, picnic tables and fire rings; vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups. Lake is non-motorized only. Reservable online with some first-come, first-served sites. --Claude
